title: st.button lost callback from a fragment > dialog > fragment
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello, since version 1.64 (previous was 1.59.2)

Some buttons doesn't get rerun in a setup with multiple layers of fragment.

fragment > dialog > fragment.

It was working on 1.59.2.
Is it expected ? should I test with a fragment key ?

Thank you

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import sys

import streamlit as st
from streamlit import runtime, session_state
from streamlit.web import cli as stcli

_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX = "_counter_value"


[USER].fragment
def _render_button_in_dialog(page_key: str) -> None:
    """Fragment: increment button rendered inside the dialog."""
    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"
    st.metric("Count", session_state[counter_key])
    if st.button("➕ Increment", key=f"{page_key}_increment_btn", type="primary"):
        session_state[counter_key] += 1
        st.rerun(scope="fragment")


[USER].fragment
def _render_button(page_key: str) -> None:
    """Fragment: open-dialog button."""
    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"

    if counter_key not in session_state:
        session_state[counter_key] = 0

    [USER].dialog("Counter", width="small")
    def _open_dialog() -> None:
        _render_button_in_dialog(page_key)

    st.button("🔢 Open Counter", key=f"{page_key}_open_btn", on_click=_open_dialog)


def launch(page_key: str = "counter") -> None:
    _render_button(page_key)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if runtime.exists():
        st.set_page_config(layout="centered", page_title="Counter Demo", page_icon="🔢")
        launch(page_key="standalone")
    else:
        sys.argv = ["streamlit", "run", sys.argv[0]]
        sys.exit(stcli.main())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

label should increment. rerun or callback triggered

### Current Behavior

no callback or rerun, button action is dropped.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17112)
I was able to reproduce this here: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-17112

This is a regression in the `fragment → dialog → fragment` nesting: the Increment button stays visible, but its click never reruns the inner fragment. `[USER].dialog` is itself a `_fragment`. The repro opens that dialog from a fragment widget’s `on_click`, so the dialog (and the nested `[USER].fragment` inside it) are registered during the callback. Since #16141 (in 1.64), callbacks bind `ThreadState.fragment_id` to the opener widget’s fragment, so those dialog/inner fragments become **descendants of the opener**. The opener then still does its default fragment rerun without calling the dialog again; `clear_stale_descendants` evicts the nested callables while the modal remains on `event_dg`. Later clicks send the evicted id and `AppSession.request_rerun` drops them. In 1.59.2 callbacks did not set `fragment_id`, so the dialog was registered as a root fragment and survived. A fragment `key` would not fix this. [#17039](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17039) (full-app-scoped dialog lifetime) likely covers this on `develop`, but its e2e opens the dialog from `if st.button()` rather than `on_click`, so that path should still be verified.

### Related Issues

- [#17011](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17011) — Same eviction class: a dialog opened from a fragment stays on screen after the parent fragment reruns, but clicks stop working. Closed by #17039; this report is the `on_click` + nested inner fragment variant.
- [#8591](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8591) — Opening a dialog from a button `on_click` historically made later dialog button clicks fail with a missing fragment id. Same callback-open pattern, without the extra inner `[USER].fragment`.
- [#10283](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10283) — `st.dialog` inside `[USER].fragment` has inconsistent lifecycle (dismiss/reopen) compared with a top-level dialog. Same feature intersection, different failure mode.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Thanks for the report [USER] 

This is the same bug as #17011. The fix is already on develop in #17039 ([Preserve dialogs across parent fragment reruns](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17039)). We re-ran this issue’s repro against current develop after that merge: Increment updates Count as expected.

It will ship in the next release after 1.65 (next week). Until then, a workaround is to open the dialog from the parent fragment body (e.g. a session-state flag) rather than from on_click, so the dialog fragment is re-registered on the parent rerun.

For example:

```
[USER].fragment
def counter_dialog():
    [USER].dialog("Counter", width="small")
    def _open_dialog():
        if "count" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state.count = 0
        st.metric("Count", st.session_state.count)
        if st.button("Increment", type="primary"):
            st.session_state.count += 1
            st.rerun(scope="fragment")
    # Open from the fragment body, not on_click.
    if st.button("Open Counter"):
        st.session_state.show_counter = True
    if st.session_state.get("show_counter"):
        _open_dialog()
counter_dialog()
```

This workaround is included in the repro app as well: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-17112
